n: Isaiah’s final chapter opens with God’s greatness: heaven is His throne and earth His footstool. What house could people build that would contain Him? Stephen quoted this before he was martyred.

f.w: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool

n: God made all of it. But the person He looks to with favor is the humble, contrite one who trembles at His word. God values a humble heart more than grand buildings.

f.w: him that is poor and of a contrite spirit
trembleth at my word
f.g: Reveres God’s word and takes it seriously.

n: For the hypocritical, sacrifices are no better than murder or pagan offerings—sacrificing an ox is like killing a man; offering incense is like praising an idol. Ritual without a right heart is offensive to God.

f.w: He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man
oblation

n: Since they chose their own ways, God will let them have the consequences they dread. When He called, no one answered.

f.w: I also will choose their delusions
f.g: I will choose their punishments—let their own choices rebound on them.

f.w: when I called, none did answer

n: A word of comfort to the faithful who tremble at God’s word: your own relatives hated and excluded you because of Me, mocking, “Let the Lord show His glory!” But He will appear to your joy, and they will be put to shame.

f.w: cast you out for my name's sake

n: Hear that uproar from the city, that voice from the temple! It is the Lord repaying His enemies.

f.w: a voice from the temple

n: An amazing image: Zion gives birth before her labor even begins—a son delivered before the pains came. Restoration comes with unexpected speed.

f.w: she was delivered of a man child

n: Who has ever heard of such a thing? Can a land be born in one day, a nation in a moment? Yet as soon as Zion went into labor, her children were born.

f.w: shall a nation be born at once?
f.g: Many have connected this to the sudden rebirth of Israel or to the rapid latter-day gathering.

n: Would God bring a birth to the very moment of delivery and then not allow it? Of course not. He finishes what He begins.

f.w: shall I cause to bring forth, and shut the womb?

n: All who love Jerusalem and mourned over her should now rejoice with her.

f.w: Rejoice ye with Jerusalem

n: Zion is pictured as a nursing mother; her children drink deeply from her comfort and abundance.

f.w: the breasts of her consolations
f.g: The comforting nourishment Zion provides, like a mother’s milk.

n: God will send peace flowing to Zion like a river and the wealth of nations like an overflowing stream. Her children will be carried on her hip and bounced on her knees.

f.w: I will extend peace to her like a river
dandled
f.g: Bounced playfully, as a parent does with a baby.

n: “As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you.” One of the most tender images of God in scripture.

f.w: As one whom his mother comforteth

n: When you see this, your heart will rejoice and your body will flourish like fresh grass. God’s hand will be clear—blessing His servants and opposing His enemies.

f.w: your bones shall flourish like an herb

n: The Lord will come in fire, with chariots like a whirlwind, bringing judgment. Scripture repeatedly connects fire with the Second Coming.

f.w: the LORD will come with fire

n: By fire and sword the Lord will judge all humanity, and many will fall.

f.w: will the LORD plead with all flesh
f.g: Enter into judgment with all people.

n: Those who “sanctify” themselves for pagan rites in gardens, following a leader in the middle, and eat pork, rodents, and other detestable things will perish together.

f.w: behind one tree in the midst
f.g: Possibly “following one in the middle”—a cult leader or priest of a pagan rite.

f.w: the mouse

n: God knows their works and thoughts. The time is coming when He will gather all nations and languages to see His glory.

f.w: I will gather all nations and tongues

n: God will set a sign among them and send survivors as messengers to distant nations—Tarshish, Put, Lud, Tubal, Javan (Greece), and faraway coastlands—to declare His glory to those who never heard. A remarkable picture of worldwide missionary work.

f.w: Tarshish, Pul, and Lud
f.g: Far western and African peoples; “Pul” likely means Put (Libya).

f.w: Javan
they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles

n: They will bring back all your brothers from every nation as an offering to the Lord—on horses, chariots, litters, mules, and camels—to Jerusalem, just as Israelites bring grain offerings in clean vessels to the temple. The gathering itself is an offering.

f.w: they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the LORD
litters
f.g: Covered chairs or couches carried on poles.

f.w: swift beasts

n: Astonishingly, God will take some of these gathered people—perhaps even from among the Gentiles—to be priests and Levites.

f.w: I will also take of them for priests and for Levites

n: As permanent as the new heavens and new earth God will make, so permanent will His people’s descendants and name be.

f.w: the new heavens and the new earth

n: Every new moon and every Sabbath, all people will come to worship the Lord. Worship becomes universal and regular.

f.w: shall all flesh come to worship before me

n: A sobering final image: outside the city lie the bodies of those who rebelled, where the worm doesn’t die and the fire isn’t quenched. Jesus used this language for the fate of the unrepentant. Isaiah ends with both hope and warning: choose the Lord.

f.w: their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched
an abhorring
f.g: Something repulsive, looked on with horror.
